t: You're standing in St James's Square, a garden square in Westminster with mostly Georgian and Neo-Georgian buildings. For its first couple of hundred years it was one of the most fashionable places to live in London. Today it holds company headquarters, including BP and Rio Tinto, four private members' clubs, the London Library and Chatham House. Many notable people lived here. The Duke of Hamilton and the Marchioness of Londonderry were born here. Two admirals, Lord Vere and the Earl of Bristol, died here, as did the Dukes of Cleveland, one an illegitimate son of Charles the Second.
